assessments.name: Thin provisioning
assessments.recommendation: Workload Factory recommends configuring thin provisioning for FSx for ONTAP volumes hosting Oracle databases. This approach optimizes storage efficiency and cost-effectiveness by allowing more logical data to be stored than physically available.

assessments.name: Autosize
assessments.recommendation: Workload Factory recommends enabling volume autogrow for FSx for ONTAP volumes for Oracle databases. This configuration enhances flexibility, availability, and scalability for Oracle databases by allowing volumes to grow dynamically to accommodate unexpected data growth, preventing space shortages and avoiding downtime if a volume runs out of space. Volume autogrow is essential when using thin provisioning.

assessments.name: Autosize mode
assessments.recommendation: Workload Factory recommends enabling volume autogrow for FSx for ONTAP volumes for Oracle databases. This configuration enhances flexibility and availability by allowing volumes to grow dynamically to accommodate unexpected data growth. This prevents space shortages and helps avoid downtime if a volume runs out of space, ensuring seamless scalability for Oracle databases. Volume autogrow is essential when using thin provisioning.

assessments.name: Block device space management
assessments.recommendation:
Workload Factory recommends configuring block device space settings for LUNs used by Oracle database instances to prevent write failures and improve space efficiency on FSx for ONTAP. This configuration applies the recommended combination of settings for thin-provisioned volumes:
- Space reservation: enabled - reserves enough space in the volume so writes to the LUN do not fail.
- Space allocation: enabled - allows FSx for ONTAP to notify the EC2 host when a volume is full and supports automatic space reclamation when the database deletes data.
- Fractional reserve: disabled - avoids unnecessary overwrite reservation, optimizing space utilization and cost effectiveness for thin provisioning.
Together, these settings help ensure predictable database behavior while minimizing wasted capacity.

assessments.name: Snapshot policy
assessments.recommendation: Workload Factory recommends disabling snapshots for FSx for ONTAP volumes for Oracle databases to save space and lower costs. Oracle snapshots should be managed externally via tools like SnapCenter, which creates application-consistent snapshots, preventing corruption during restoration.

assessments.name: Snapshot copy reserve
assessments.recommendation: Workload Factory recommends that capacity isnt reserved for snapshots on FSx for ONTAP volumes used by databases, making the entire volume capacity available for active data and any snapshots that are created.

assessments.name: Snapshot autodelete
assessments.recommendation: Workload Factory recommends configuring the snapshot autodelete feature in FSx for ONTAP for Oracle databases to delete older snapshots first. This feature is designed to automatically manage snapshot storage by deleting the oldest snapshots when a volume approaches its capacity limit. This configuration helps in thin-provisioned environments, where more logical storage is allocated than physically available.

assessments.name: Space management
assessments.recommendation: Workload Factory recommends configuring space management to prioritize volume expansion over snapshot deletion for thin-provisioned FSx for ONTAP volumes with volume autogrow enabled.

assessments.name: Cold data tiering
assessments.recommendation: Workload Factory recommends enabling tiering for some Oracle database volumes on Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP where appropriate, to move cold data to lower-cost capacity storage and reduce overall storage costs, while keeping active database data on high-performance SSDs to preserve critical performance. Recommended policies are based on the data type in each volume, with tiering disabled (none) for data files and redo logs, and auto for archive logs. For archive/FRA volumes, it is also recommended to set an appropriate cooling period before data is tiered—typically 2 days for compressed backups and 14 days for uncompressed backups—to balance cost efficiency and performance.

configDetails.recommendedNote: 14 when FRA is enabled and RMAN compression is disabled; not assessed on non-archive volumes

assessments.name: Storage efficiencies
assessments.recommendation: Workload Factory recommends implementing storage efficiencies—compression, compaction, and deduplication—in NetApp ONTAP for Oracle database environments to significantly reduce storage footprint, lower costs, and optimize resource utilization while maintaining performance. Tailored settings for each volume type ensure alignment with Oracle's I/O patterns: Data and archive Volumes benefit from inline adaptive compression (8KB), compaction and deduplication while Redo Log Volumes prioritize performance with minimal savings from these features.

configDetails.recommendedNote: both is also acceptable for non-log-files volumes

assessments.name: NFS root only
assessments.recommendation: Workload Factory recommends disabling the nfs-rootonly parameter for dNFS. ONTAPs nfs-rootonly setting restricts NFS connections to privileged ports (<1024). Since dNFS processes in NFSv4+ do not run as root and use higher ports, disabling this parameter allows necessary connections.

assessments.name: Export policy
assessments.recommendation: Workload Factory recommends ensuring that if Oracle binaries are located on an NFS share, the export policy includes superuser and setuid permissions.Superuser (root) access allows NFS clients to map as root, needed for binary execution.

assessments.name: dNFS enabled
assessments.recommendation: Workload Factory recommends enabling Direct NFS (dNFS) for your Oracle environment. Enabling dNFS can improve database performance and simplify NFS storage management by allowing Oracle to manage NFS I/O directly.

assessments.name: dNFS consistent IP resolution
assessments.recommendation: Workload Factory recommends avoiding the use of Direct NFS (dNFS) with any type of round-robin name resolution, including DNS, DDNS, NIS, or any other method. This includes the DNS load balancing feature available in ONTAP. Ensuring consistent IP address resolution is crucial for maintaining database stability and preventing potential crashes or data corruption.

assessments.name: dNFS configuration file
assessments.recommendation: Workload Factory recommends verifying and optimizing the oranfstab file content to ensure proper Direct NFS (dNFS) usage. The oranfstab file is essential for configuring advanced dNFS features such as multipathing and specific NFS options. Proper configuration ensures efficient data access and management.

assessments.name: dNFS no shared cache
assessments.recommendation: Workload Factory recommends configuring the nosharecache mount option for environments where Direct NFS (dNFS) is enabled, and a source volume is mounted more than once on a single server with nested NFS mounts. This configuration prevents cache sharing between mounts, ensuring data consistency and optimal performance.

assessments.name: Filesystems I/O options
assessments.recommendation: Workload Factory recommends setting the filesystemio_options parameter to SETALL for optimal I/O performance with Oracle databases on NFS. This setting enables both asynchronous I/O and direct I/O, which can significantly improve database performance.

assessments.name: TCP advanced options
assessments.recommendation: Workload Factory recommends configuring TCP advanced options including window scaling, selective acknowledgments, and timestamps for optimal NFS performance with Oracle databases.

assessments.name: Transparent huge pages
assessments.recommendation: Workload Factory recommends disabling transparent huge pages for Oracle databases. Transparent huge pages can cause performance issues and memory fragmentation for Oracle workloads.

assessments.name: Multiblock read count
assessments.recommendation: Workload Factory recommends configuring db_file_multiblock_read_count for Oracle databases on NFS to optimize full table scan performance. The recommended value depends on your block size and workload characteristics.

assessments.name: Archive placement
assessments.recommendation: Placing archive logs on a dedicated volume enhances performance and recovery processes. This isolation prevents high I/O demands from interfering with other operations, ensuring efficient logging, sorting, and reliable backup and recovery.

assessments.name: Data files placement
assessments.recommendation: Placing data files on a dedicated volume or shared with control files boosts performance by isolating their random I/O from redo or archive log writes, reducing contention. This separation allows you to benefit from customized snapshot configurations, tiering policies, and efficiency mechanisms to optimize performance and cost.

assessments.name: Control files placement
assessments.recommendation: Oracle strongly recommends multiplexing control files to avoid a single point of failure in production environments. Maintain at least two, preferably three, control file copies across separate volumes or disks to enhance redundancy and reduce the risk of losing all copies. Control files can be placed on a dedicated volume or shared with redo logs or data files, but avoid placing them on volumes tiered to object storage, such as archive volumes, as its slower access pattern is incompatible with control file performance needs.

assessments.name: Redo logs placement
assessments.recommendation: Placing redo logs, whether multiplexed or not, on a dedicated volume or shared with temp/control files isolates their high-write I/O from data file transactions, improving performance. Each multiplexed redo log copy should reside on a separate volume for redundancy. Frequent changes make redo logs unsuitable for snapshotted volumes, like data volumes, as they inflate snapshot sizes. Redo logs must not be placed on volumes tiered to object storage, such as archive volumes, as their frequent updates are incompatible with object storages slower access patterns. This separation enables customized efficiency mechanisms and tiering configurations for optimal database performance and cost efficiency.

assessments.name: Swap space
assessments.recommendation: Proper swap sizing ensures that the system can handle memory pressure gracefully, avoiding potential performance degradation or system crashes.

assessments.name: File system headroom
assessments.recommendation: To optimize storage performance, provision file system capacity as 1.2 times of total size of provisioned volume.

assessments.name: Operating system patch
assessments.recommendation: Critical security patches are missing. We recommend applying the latest patches to ensure your database infrastructure is secure and up-to-date.

assessments.name: Backup configuration
assessments.recommendation: Backup Configuration recommendation: Enable FSx Backup or AWS Backup for Oracle database volumes to support data retention and compliance. If using both, consider removing redundant backups manually.

assessments.name: Cross-Region Replication (CRR)
assessments.recommendation: Workload Factory recommends enabling Cross-Region Replication (CRR) for your FSx for ONTAP filesystems serving Oracle. CRR ensures that your data is replicated to another AWS region, providing enhanced data durability and availability. It is recommended to configure CRR for disaster recovery and compliance requirements. Replicating redo logs (when applicable) can also assist with recovery to a specific point in time.

assessments.name: Application-consistent snapshots
assessments.recommendation: Use application-consistent snapshots with NetApp SnapCenter to take accurate, reliable snapshots of your volume data at a specific moment in time. This keeps your apps running smoothly and your data safe. SnapCenter makes backups easier and helps you restore data quickly and correctly, reducing downtime and protecting your most important workloads.

assessments.name: Oracle critical security patch
assessments.recommendation: Oracle Critical Patch Updates (CPUs) include security fixes for supported self-managed Oracle databases. Installing the latest patch helps protect your database from vulnerabilities and improves system reliability.

assessments.name: Clone cleanup
assessments.recommendation: Old clones can incur significant costs. Consider deleting these clones to optimize your storage expenses.

assessments.name: Multipath I/O
assessments.recommendation: Workload Factory recommends enabling and configuring multipath I/O for Oracle database hosts using iSCSI to ensure redundancy and improve storage performance.

assessments.name: Host utilities
assessments.recommendation: Workload Factory recommends installing NetApp Linux Host Utilities on Oracle database hosts. Host utilities provide optimized multipath settings and improved storage connectivity for NetApp storage systems.

assessments.name: Multipath I/O sessions
assessments.recommendation: Workload Factory recommends configuring the optimal number of iSCSI sessions per target for Oracle database hosts to maximize throughput and redundancy.

assessments.name: iSCSI replacement timeout
assessments.recommendation: Workload Factory recommends configuring the iSCSI replacement timeout to an appropriate value for Oracle database hosts to prevent unnecessary session timeouts during storage failover.

assessments.name: Multipath friendly names
assessments.recommendation: Workload Factory recommends disabling multipath friendly names for Oracle database hosts to ensure consistent device naming based on WWIDs.

assessments.name: Multipath configuration
assessments.recommendation: Workload Factory strongly recommends that the multipath configuration file (/etc/multipath.conf) be properly configured with NetApp recommended settings for ONTAP block devices, as this is critical for reliable path management, optimal performance, and compatibility with ONTAP storage systems. In addition, installing the Device Mapper Multipath package on all database hosts that connect to ONTAP storage via iSCSI enables multipath I/O, providing redundancy, failover, and resilient storage connectivity for Oracle databases. This combined approach ensures robust and dependable integration with ONTAP storage.

assessments.name: ASM setup
assessments.recommendation: Workload Factory recommends verifying that Oracle ASM is properly configured for use with FSx for ONTAP. Proper ASM setup ensures optimal storage management and performance for Oracle databases.

assessments.name: ASM external redundancy
assessments.recommendation: Workload Factory recommends configuring ASM disk groups with external redundancy when using FSx for ONTAP, which provides its own redundancy. Using ASM internal redundancy would mirror data unnecessarily, consuming double the storage.

assessments.name: AFD logical block size
assessments.recommendation: Workload Factory recommends verifying that the AFD (ASM Filter Driver) logical block size is correctly configured for Oracle ASM disk groups. Incorrect block size can lead to I/O alignment issues and performance degradation.

assessments.name: ASMLib logical block size
assessments.recommendation: Workload Factory recommends verifying that the ASMLib logical block size is correctly configured for Oracle ASM disk groups. Incorrect block size can lead to I/O alignment issues and performance degradation.
